name: United Kingdom
title: Fully funded master's and PhDs in the UK: the scholarships that pay for everything
meta_title: Fully funded master's and PhDs in the UK for international students
lede: UK tuition for international students is high, so the UK is a country you reach through a scholarship. Luckily it has some of the world's best-known full awards: Chevening, Commonwealth, Gates Cambridge, Rhodes and the Mastercard Foundation programme at Cambridge.
description: Study in the UK for free: Chevening, Commonwealth, Gates Cambridge, Rhodes and Mastercard Foundation scholarships, plus application fees and visa costs.
card: High fees, but the strongest line-up of full scholarships anywhere: Chevening, Commonwealth, Gates, Rhodes.

sections.h: Why the UK needs a scholarship
sections.html: International students pay international tuition at UK universities, often well above £20,000 a year for a master's, and more for laboratory subjects. UK master's degrees are usually just one year, though, so a single award can fund a complete degree, which is exactly what the major scholarships do.

Undergraduates apply through UCAS: for 2027 entry, one fee of £34.50 covers up to five choices. For a master's or PhD you apply to each university, and each sets its own fee.

UniversityApplication feeWaivers
Oxford£75 for taught courses; £20 for research coursesResidents of listed low-income countries, and refugees and displaced people
Cambridge£85 per master's application; £20 for doctoral courses, covering up to 7 applicationsAutomatic for nationals of listed countries who have lived there since birth; African applicants to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program can ask by 20 November 2026
Imperial College London£90 for most master's; £125 for Business School MSc coursesOn request, if you are in financial difficulty
UCL£90; £160 for some business master'sOnly for hardship caused by conflict or displacement

At the University of Manchester, only eight Business School MSc courses charge a fee (£60); the school's other courses are free to apply to.

The Oxford and Cambridge lists are mostly the world's poorest countries, such as Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Uganda and Zambia. Ghana, Nigeria and Kenya are not on either list. Always ask for a waiver before you pay: neither Cambridge nor Imperial can waive a fee that has already been paid.

Compare other countries in our guide to universities with no application fee.

sections.h: Visa costs and proof of funds
sections.html: A UK Student visa requires you to show money for living costs for up to nine months: £1,529 a month in London or £1,171 a month elsewhere for applications from 11 November 2025. You also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (£776 a year for students) and the visa fee. Full scholarships such as Chevening and Commonwealth normally cover these or count as your financial evidence. Check your award letter.

Chevening and Commonwealth scholars must return to their home country after the award (two years for Chevening), and Commonwealth scholars cannot switch to the Graduate visa. If staying to work in the UK matters to you, Gates Cambridge and Rhodes have no such rule. Read each award's terms before applying.

On a Student visa for a degree-level course at a university, you may work up to 20 hours a week in term time, counting every job together, and full time outside term. Courses below degree level allow 10 hours a week. Your university may set lower limits.

sections.h: After you graduate: the Graduate visa
sections.html: The Graduate visa lets you stay and work, or look for work, after a UK degree. For bachelor's and master's graduates it lasts two years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, and 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027. After a PhD it lasts three years. Remember that Chevening and Commonwealth scholars must go home after their award.

faq.q: How much does it cost to apply to a UK university?
faq.a: Undergraduate applications through UCAS cost £34.50 for up to five choices for 2027 entry. Postgraduate fees are set by each university: £75 at Oxford for taught courses, £85 at Cambridge for a master's, and £90 at Imperial and UCL.

faq.q: Can I get my UK application fee waived?
faq.a: Oxford waives it for residents of listed low-income countries, and Cambridge for nationals of listed countries who have lived there since birth; Ghana, Nigeria and Kenya are not on either list. Imperial considers waivers for financial difficulty. Ask before you pay.

faq.q: How much money do I need for a UK Student visa?
faq.a: £1,529 a month for up to nine months in London, or £1,171 a month elsewhere, on top of any unpaid tuition. A full scholarship often counts as your evidence.

faq.q: Can I work while studying in the UK?
faq.a: At degree level, up to 20 hours a week in term and full time in the holidays.

faq.q: How long is the UK Graduate visa?
faq.a: Two years if you apply by 31 December 2026 and 18 months from 1 January 2027, for bachelor's and master's graduates; three years after a PhD.
